_what_this_is: Hosts that may NOT supply evidence for a grounded market bet. Everything not listed is allowed. This replaces config/news_whitelist.json, which was doing source sanitation the verbatim gate already does better.
_why_it_flipped: R43 requires the SIGNAL to be an EXACT SUBSTRING of a retrieved snippet. That is the fabrication guard, and it does not care who published the snippet — a quote is either in the document or it is not. The whitelist was therefore filtering on a property the bet does not consume, and on 2026-09-07 it refused all three assets while the real constraints were a broken date parser and a holiday weekend. Filter by the property you actually consume, at its granularity.
_what_a_blacklist_is_still_for: Poison, not viewpoints. Two things a verbatim quote cannot protect against: PROMPT INJECTION, where user-generated text contains instructions aimed at the model, and CONTENT FARMS, where the 'quote' is machine-spun text with no author. Both are properties of the HOST, so the host is the right granularity for them.
_what_this_is_NOT_for: Quality, tone, house style, or whether a source is bullish. A site being shallow is not a reason to block it — the bet is graded by reality, not by the pedigree of its reason. If a host is here because somebody disliked its conclusions, that is a bug in this file.
_classes_are_metadata_now: Each known host keeps its reporter_independence class from the four declared in config/reporter_independence.json — self_reported, independent, adversarial, unknown. The class is passed to the model as part of the evidence, because the SOURCE TYPE IS PART OF THE MARKET SIGNAL: a wire report and a company press release move a price differently. It is NEVER a gate. An unknown host is class 'unknown' and is allowed.
_who_owns_it: A human. A generated patch that added a host here would be the system choosing what it is allowed to read.

reddit.com.why: user-generated; a top comment can contain instructions aimed at the model

medium.com.why: open publishing platform; no editorial chain

substack.com.why: open publishing platform; no editorial chain

wikipedia.org.why: user-editable at any moment; not a dated report

en.wikipedia.org.why: user-editable at any moment; not a dated report

investorplace.com.why: high-volume SEO output with thin sourcing

247wallst.com.why: high-volume SEO output with thin sourcing

_blocked_suffixes_note: Subdomain-hosted open publishing. A suffix match here is deliberate: anyone can create one of these in a minute, so the host name carries no accountability.
_a_broker_is_self_reported: A broker publishing market commentary has a position in people trading. That is the taxonomy's 'the measured entity produces the statistic' shape, and it is why the class travels with the evidence into the prompt.
_adversarial_here_means_stake: fool.com and seekingalpha carry authors with disclosed positions arguing a side. The class says so; it does not block them. An argued case is a real market signal.
_the_three_date_states: dated and inside max_age_hours -> CITABLE. dated and outside -> DROPPED, because the date is a real claim and it failed. UNDATED -> DOWNGRADED to context-only, not dropped: usable as a citation only when the citable pool is empty, and a bet grounded that way is flagged 'ungrounded-citation'. Absence of a date is not evidence of staleness, but it is not evidence of freshness either.
